One of the things I find most fascinating about AI  is image generation. You may take this for granted but the thing dey burst my head I swear down 🔥🥰😅

Especially when it comes to photoshoots, studio pictures, avatars and creative photography.

Think about it.

A few years ago, if you wanted to see yourself in five different studio concepts, different outfits, different environments and different creative directions, you would need a photographer, studio, clothes, makeup, lighting, editing and probably multiple sessions.

Today, with the right picture, the right idea and the right prompt, you can bring that imagination to life with AI.

And for me, this is bigger than simply saying, “You don’t have to pay for a studio photoshoot.”
Just like the image attached to this post .. this is AI and that’s my product VALOAI on the jersey 

Seee ehn 

It is about creative freedom. You can imagine something and actually see yourself in it.

A corporate executive photoshoot.

A podcast studio.

A fashion campaign.

A cinematic scene.

A professional website headshot.

An avatar.

A flyer for your business.

A product campaign.

Entertainment content.

Personal branding.

You can experiment with concepts that would normally be difficult, expensive or almost impossible to produce physically.

Someone who cannot afford a professional studio can now create quality images.

But even someone who can afford the studio now has another powerful creative tool. Because AI gives you the ability to explore ideas before they ever exist in the real world.

That is what excites me.

The combination of technology + imagination + creativity.

AI image generation has become so good that sometimes you look at what you created and think:
“This is too good to be true.” 

But like every powerful AI tool, your result depends heavily on knowing how to use it.

The reference images you use.

How you describe what you want.

How you structure your prompts.

How you maintain your face and body consistency.

Lighting.

Camera angles.

Composition.

Styling.

Realism.

All these things matter.

GPT IMAGE 2 + MIINIMAX H3 WITH PROMPTS

What if your AI tools became a cinematic universe? 

I wanted to try something a little different with MiniMax H3 and create a commercial for LOVART AI that feels more like a fashion campaign than a typical tech ad.

I put my virtual influencer, Alexa Grey, in LOVART’s bright yellow and white colors and built the whole concept around text, characters and visual storytelling.

One thing I really wanted to explore was how far I could push the typography.

MiniMax prompts use editorial typography, characters crossing through letters, billboards, graphic cards, oversized text, parallax and visual transitions.

So instead of simply putting a model name on screen, I made the lettering part of the world.

Alexa walks through giant words.
Characters move around the typography.
Billboards become cinematic scenes.
Letters transform into environments.
Graphic cards transition into completely different worlds.

And then I brought the AI models into the story:

The goal was to make everything feel connected — characters, typography, billboards, environments and AI models all living inside the same creative universe.

And at the end, it all comes together as: 
LOVART AI: YOUR AI CREATIVE STUDIO.

No dialogue. No voiceover.

Just visuals, music, typography, and motion.
